claude.sample_unit: consultations (each with clinician, zero-shot AI, and prompted AI replies)

links.outcome: Terminology explanation frequency per reply across clinician, unprompted AI, and prompted AI
links.effect: Terminology explanations per reply: clinician 0.301, unprompted AI 1.337, prompted AI 1.981; replies with no explanation fell from 81.1% (clinician) to 38.3% (unprompted) to 15.3% (prompted).
links.quote: With the narrative prompt, explanation density increased further to 1.981 (95% CI [1.901, 2.061]), while the share of replies offering no explanation fell to 15.3% (Wilson 95% CI [0.132, 0.177]).

links.outcome: Coded empathy (verbal support, emotion-symptom linkage) in clinician vs zero-shot vs narrative-prompted LLM replies
links.effect: Verbal empathy per reply: 0.092 clinician, 0.434 unprompted, 1.99 prompted. Emotion-symptom linkage: 2.6%, 14.4%, 99.1%.
links.quote: Under narrative prompting, however, the probability becomes near-universal (99.1%; 95% CI 98.3–99.5%).

unlisted_practices: Narrative-based prompting (storytelling, empathy, personalization, clarity) to improve patient-facing communication features of LLM replies

links.effect: Prompted AI highest; narrative frequency 3.669 vs doctor 0.031 and unprompted 0.012; verbal empathy 1.99 vs 0.092 and 0.434.
links.quote: Across the reported communication measures, the prompted model showed the most favorable overall pattern, with higher narrative-device use, empathic support, contextual tailoring, and terminology explanation, alongside more frequent consideration of patient preferences and markedly higher rates of emotion-symptom linkage and the presence of a patient-centered narrative framework.

links.effect: Emotion–symptom linkage: prompted 99.1% (95% CI 98.3–99.5%) vs unprompted 14.4%, physicians 2.6%.
links.quote: Under narrative prompting, however, the probability becomes near-universal (99.1%; 95% CI 98.3–99.5%).
